Reference Manual Technical Note
Scenarios
UKCP18 presets are central estimates (50th percentile) under RCP8.5 for Wales, with seasonally-structured perturbations applied to the paper's Winter (Nov–Mar) and Summer (May–Sep) climatologies. The equilibrium framework resolves seasonal Delta-h equilibria but not within-year dynamical trajectories.

Specific yield (storage)
Fetter
Fetter (lower bound): C1 8%, C2–C5 12% — conservative literature values from Fetter (2001).
WTF (upper bound): per-well WTF medians (scripts 17/18), clamped to the cluster floor. Monthly WTF overestimates Sy through capillary-fringe conflation (Healy & Cook 2002), so these values represent an empirical ceiling.
What this changes: the Mean Sy and Storage shift rows in the table, the Sy and Storage cards for every cluster and for the site, and the per-well Sy in the map tooltip. Storage shift is Δh × Sy, in mm of equivalent water column, so switching endpoint rescales every storage figure on the page. It does not change Δh, which the state-space model fits on heads and never consumes an absolute Sy.

Groundwater surface — masked to site boundary

Interpretation note: The surface shown is an interpolated statistical estimate (IDW, k=8 nearest neighbours), not a calibrated groundwater flow simulation. It reflects the per-well steady-state response of the fitted state-space model to the selected scenario perturbations. Spatial patterns between wells are smoothed; localised features such as perched water tables or bedrock contacts are not resolved. See the Technical Note below and the manuscript (Section 3.6) for full methodological detail.

Head by cluster

Cluster summary

ΔMSL5 is the mean change in monthly water level over the spring window (March–May), the 5-year mean spring water level metric of van Willegen et al. (2025) and the best-performing published predictor of dune-slack vegetation response. It is computed as a pure-climate perturbation (β₁·ΔP − β₂·ΔPET) and is independent of the season tab. Canopy interception is not applied to this row; the other rows above (Δ head, storage shift, Pₑₑ, PET draw) do apply it for the forest clusters (C4, C5) under their seasonal P/PET multipliers, so the two formulations sit side-by-side and may disagree slightly for C4 and C5 under climate-change presets. MSL5 is in any case a vegetation predictor primarily relevant to the open dune-slack clusters C1–C3.
